edges.description: Sustained oxypurinol exposure amplifies the concentration-dependent generation of drug-specific T cells.
Activated cytotoxic lymphocytes release mediators that kill keratinocytes.
Systemic immune activation contributes to the influenza-like febrile prodrome, although the intervening cytokine pathway is not specified here.
Confluent keratinocyte death produces full-thickness epidermal necrosis.
Loss of the epidermal barrier produces systemic consequences.
Epidermal necrolysis directly manifests as skin detachment.
Dermo-epidermal separation manifests clinically as blistering.
Mucosal epithelial necrolysis produces painful oral erosions.
Ocular-surface involvement produces acute conjunctival inflammation.
Genital mucosal epithelial injury produces erosions.

Allopurinol itself is not the antigenic species. It is metabolized to oxypurinol, which is what engages peptide-HLA complexes at the cell surface, so the prescribed exposure reaches this node through its metabolite.

evidence.reference_title: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis in the Era of Systems Medicine.
evidence.snippet: severe mucocutaneous bullous disorders characterized by widespread skin and mucosal necrosis and detachment, which are most commonly triggered by medications

nodes.description: Therapeutic exposure to allopurinol (for gout/hyperuricemia) is the precipitating exposure. In EuroSCAR, risk was concentrated in the first eight weeks and was higher at daily doses of at least 200 mg.

evidence.reference_title: HLA-B*5801 allele as a genetic marker for severe cutaneous adverse reactions caused by allopurinol.
evidence.snippet: Allopurinol, a commonly prescribed medication for gout and hyperuricemia, is a frequent cause of severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCAR), which include the drug hypersensitivity syndrome, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis.

evidence.reference_title: Allopurinol is the most common cause of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis in Europe and Israel.
evidence.snippet: Daily doses equal to or greater than 200 mg were associated with a higher risk (adjusted odds ratio = 36, 95% confidence interval: 17-76) than lower doses (adjusted odds ratio = 3.0, 95% confidence interval: 1.1-8.4). The risk was restricted to short-term use (<or=8 weeks).

nodes.description: Acute ocular-surface inflammation may accompany the mucocutaneous eruption; ocular disease can also produce important long-term sequelae.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and treatment of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis with ocular complications.
evidence.snippet: Acute conjunctivitis and oral and nail involvements were reported in all patients who remembered the details. Acute conjunctivitis occurred before the skin eruptions in 42 patients and simultaneously in 21 patients, whereas only 1 patient reported posteruption conjunctivitis.

nodes.description: Oxypurinol-specific CD8 T cells are activated in a concentration-dependent response favored by HLA-B*58:01, then expand as the effector population that targets keratinocytes. NK cells also participate in the convergent SJS/TEN effector response.

evidence.reference_title: Allopurinol hypersensitivity is primarily mediated by dose-dependent oxypurinol-specific T cell response.
evidence.snippet: Allopurinol allergic patients are primarily sensitized to oxypurinol in a dose-dependent manner. TCL induction data show that both the presence of HLA-B*58:01 allele and high concentration of drug are important for the generation of drug-specific T cells.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis and management of Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis.
evidence.snippet: Drug-specific CD8 T-cells and natural killer cells are thought to be the major inducers of keratinocyte apoptosis via release of soluble cytotoxic mediators, including Fas ligand, perforin/granzyme, tumor necrosis factor, and granulysin.

evidence.snippet: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS-TEN) and erythema multiforme (EM) often present with clinically similar features in the oral mucosa: classically widespread mucosal erosions or ulceration.

nodes.description: Fever occurs in the influenza-like prodrome before the painful cutaneous and mucous-membrane lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Current Perspectives on Stevens-Johnson Syndrome and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis.
evidence.snippet: Nasopharyngeal, esophageal, and genital mucosal involvement with blisters, erosions as well as secondary development of strictures also play a role.

evidence.snippet: although HLA-B*58:01 was found to be associated with allopurinol-induced SCARs, generalizing findings from previous studies, the allele was absent in more than one-third of the patient cohort and is therefore an incomplete indicator of risk.

nodes.description: Activated lymphocytes release granulysin, Fas ligand, and perforin/granzyme, driving keratinocyte apoptosis and necroptosis — the central effector lesion of allopurinol SJS/TEN and the key conformance target of the SCAR module.

evidence.reference_title: Immunological response in Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.
evidence.snippet: With regard to keratinocyte death, several cell death mediators, such as FasL, granulysin and annexin A1, have been proposed as playing a role in SJS/TEN pathogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: A Review of the Pathogenesis of Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis.
evidence.snippet: Apoptosis or necroptosis causes keratinocytes to lose their shape and adhesion, and necrosis predominates within a few days.

nodes.description: Extensive epidermal and mucosal detachment causes skin-barrier failure with high morbidity and mortality, the defining consequence of allopurinol SJS/TEN.

evidence.snippet: immunologically mediated cutaneous adverse reaction characterized by mucous membrane and epidermal detachment, with a mortality ranging from 15% to 25%

nodes.description: Oxypurinol forms a labile interaction with peptide/HLA complexes at the cell surface and can activate drug-reactive T cells without intracellular antigen processing. HLA-B*58:01 strongly favors this response but is not required in every affected patient.

evidence.snippet: Poor renal function was significantly associated with the delayed clearance of plasma oxypurinol, and increased the risk of allopurinol-SCAR (p<0.001, OR (95% CI) 8.0 (3.9 to 17)).

nodes.description: Poor renal function delays oxypurinol clearance, increasing exposure to the metabolite that drives the dose-dependent T-cell response and worsening prognosis in allopurinol-SCAR, including SJS/TEN.
